messages:
josh: Heads-up — we're seeing a cluster-wide spike in GPU provisioning failures in us-west1-b over the last 90m. failures correlate with huge local NVMe IO bursts during node boot.
claire: yea saw it. provisioning queue stalls, kube logs show nodes stuck at image unpack / disk io. GPU launch rate dropped ~18% in the window.
tariq: digging telemetry — background vacuum/garbage-reclaim process (vacuum-runner) kicked off across nodes at 03:02 UTC and hit sustained IOPS spikes (p95 iops ~110k, avg latency 12ms). looks like it overlaps with our typical batch-provision window.
emily: vacuum-runner runs every 6h by default, single schedule across all AZs. that's the problem — simultaneous work across replicas.
josh: sample `iostat` from a repro node:
```
Device            tps  kB_read/s  kB_wrtn/s  await
nvme0n1         12500     45000     98000    11.8
```
These numbers push the disk scheduler into severe queuing and block image unpack.
claire: consequence: nodes fail healthchecks, kube evicts pods, GPUs sit idle while disk drains. we've seen ~30 wasted GPU-minutes per incident so far.
tariq: short-term mitigation idea: stagger vacuum windows per-az and throttle concurrent vacuum workers. we can also add an IO cap flag in vacuum-runner like `--max-io-kbps=200000` or `--max-workers=4`.
emily: long-term we should implement IO reservation for provisioning path (cgroups for `containerd`/image pulls) so background janitors can't fully saturate device. also consider trimming janitor scheduling to off-peak.
josh: plan for immediate action:
- gate: push a config patch to vacuum-runner to add `--max-workers` and `--stagger-by-az` (canary in us-west1-b tonight)
- emergency: add alert that fires when `gpu_provision_wait_seconds > 30` AND `nvme_avg_lat_ms > 8`
- mitigation script: `admin/pause_vacuum --node <id>` to temporarily pause jobs on nodes with >5 prov fails/hr

ops-bot: deploybot: I scheduled a canary deploy of vacuum-runner config to us-west1-b at 02:30 UTC. Tracking: deploy/3842024200-canary-vacuum-config
claire: cost tradeoff note: if we add IO reservations and reduce packing density, we expect ~4-7% higher host count to maintain throughput — ballpark +$8k/mo for prod fleet. still cheaper than wasted GPU time.
tariq: after canary we should run a 6h window test with synthetic provisioning to validate no regressions. i'll add a quick harness and post results.
emily: also let's add an aggregator metric for "background_io_fraction" so we can correlate reclaim activity vs provisioning latency automatically.
josh: ok i'll own the canary + postmortem after test. if all good we'll roll config to other regions with stagger schedule.
claire: nice. once rolled, follow-up work: implement per-az maintenance windows and kernel-level blkio cgroup reservations (RFC tracked in eng-infra board).
ops-bot: incident-bot: Created incident INC-3842024200 for tracking provisioning impact; link: https://incidents.internal/INC-3842024200
josh: thanks — i'll update with canary metrics tomorrow. :thumbsup:
